hypothesis: At N=64, as at N=128, the best-layer force margin keeps creeping up over long training and approaches a ceiling, and that ceiling is higher than at N=128. With seeds 20-21, architecture and data matched to exp-20261013-001741-c9dc and exp-20261013-031820-c873 (4 layers, d_model=64, e in [0, 0.5], m2 in [0.1, 1], best-of-3 controls) and training extended to 12000 steps, N=64 force ends clearly above the N=128 12000-step values (0.193 for seed 20, 0.197 for seed 21). So the N=64 vs N=128 gap persists at every training length. Margins are read from the per-checkpoint trajectory using unrounded values against a strict >= required_margin bar, with force taken at its best layer at each checkpoint. If either seed's step-3000 force margin differs by more than 0.03 from the 3000-step run of the same seed (0.215 for seed 20, 0.261 for seed 21), within-run growth is the primary measure and cross-run comparisons are reported as horizon-confounded.
expected_if_true: In both seeds the final (step-12000) best-layer force margin is >= 0.23, at least 0.03 above the same seed's N=128 12000-step value (0.193 / 0.197). Force gain from step 6000 to 12000 is <= 0.04. accel_step's headroom-normalised margin stays in [0.62, 0.77].
expected_if_false: In at least one seed the final force margin is <= 0.21, i.e. within 0.015 of that seed's N=128 12000-step value, so N=128 converges to the N=64 level and the gap is a growth-rate effect only. Alternatively, force keeps gaining >= 0.05 from step 6000 to 12000 in both seeds, which would mean neither N has reached its ceiling and the comparison is unresolved.
